summary:
I wrote the hair plan for cat1 as two files: the follicle palette (JSON) and fur_plan.md. Nothing has been built or proven yet; both files are a spec.

**Palette contents.** It has 15 hair types:
- body coat: white guard, two lilac guard types (stripe hairs and the lighter hairs between stripes), awn, down, and the hairs on the upper eyelid margin;
- ear: furnishings, tip wisp, sparse hair on the inner pinna skin, ear back;
- whiskers: mystacial (lip), supraorbital (above the eye), genal (cheek), chin, carpal (wrist).

Each type has base diameter, taper, length, crimp, stiffness, colour along the shaft, and a source with a confidence level.

The map has 21 regions, each with density per mm2, the guard/awn/down split, pigment and hair direction. The ear canal has zero hair. The inner pinna is no longer furless: it gets sparse fine hair, as C14 asks.

**Whiskers (C13).**
- Layout: 12 per side, 4 rows of 3, positioned on the whisker pad using the Phase 1 root spread. Two right-side Tripo roots at mouth-corner height look merged with the lip and are not used.
- Length: 30-66 mm, longer toward the back. The longest whisker in the photo is at least 61 mm, measured flat in the image. Tripo's 16-26 mm whiskers are cut-off baked shapes and are not used.
- Taper: base-to-tip radius ratio 7-13, from Williams & Kramer 2010.
- Curve: flat at the base, bending toward the tip (Luo & Hartmann 2023, 228 cat whiskers).
- Base diameter: no measured cat value exists in anything I could reach. I used a rat formula (Belli 2017), giving 125-212 um, with an allowed range of 110-320 um. Confidence is low.
- Roots sit 3 mm under the skin (estimate).
- Other groups: supraorbital 2-6 per side, 18-35 mm (2-3 visible in the photo); genal 1-3 (a photo hint only); chin 2-5 (estimate); carpal 4-6 at 20-30 mm on the fore legs (IMAIOS).

**Ear hair (C14).**
- Furnishings: about 11 mm (7-16), white, up and outward from the inner margin; the photo shows them densely over the inner half of each ear.
- Tips: the photo shows a small wisp of about 5-8 hairs sticking out 2-4 mm. There is no lynx-type tuft.
- Ear backs: short dense fur, 4 mm. The photo does not show the backs, so their lilac colour comes from the colourpoint rule and is flagged.

**What the photo shows that differs from the brief.**
- **Legs and paws are white.** So are the muzzle, chin, throat and chest. Lilac appears only on the forehead stripes, the eye surround and cheek bars, the whole tail (about 5 rings and a dark tip), and possibly a faint patch on the back of the thigh. The brief listed legs/paws as points.
- **Image scale.** At the face I measure 0.35-0.38 mm per pixel, from the eye spacing and the frozen camera. coat.json uses 0.27 mm per pixel, which does not fit the face. Someone needs to check which reference each number came from.

**Blender (version 5.2.1, read-only query).** The body coat uses hair curves, not particle hair. Guides come from the existing groom.py code. Geometry Nodes then generate the rest at the palette's density, grouped so they don't blend across hair partings. Whiskers are separate curves, one per follicle, adapted from accessories.py. I have not yet confirmed that the Interpolate Curves node exists in 5.2.

**Full density will not fit in memory.** The palette density gives about 23 M hairs on roughly 2,150-2,350 cm2 of skin. That is about 4 GB of curve data before Cycles makes its own copy, too much for this 16 GB machine. The plan uses three tiers:
- small patches at full density, for the density check (C10);
- a full-body render with guard, awn, ear hair and whiskers at full density, and the undercoat at a stated fraction picked by a memory test (starting at 25%);
- a viewport that shows only part of the hair, with the fraction per type stored on the object.

**Checks.** C8 (fur tips vs the Tripo envelope) and C9 (hair direction vs the photo) reuse existing tools. C10, C13 and C14 each need a small new tool. Each check gets planted failures to catch before it counts.

**Research gaps.**
- No primary-source cat hair density per area. The palette uses coat.json's popular-article figure (about 9,300/cm2 on the back). My rough cross-check from hair growth rates gives 4,700-9,500/cm2.
- No cat whisker base diameter (see above).
- Hair direction on the face sides, around the eyes and on the ears has no source; the photo's hair-flow measurement decides there, otherwise the built-in hair-tract directions apply.
- Two papers that might have had the missing numbers were blocked: the Noel & Hu supplement and Dougill et al. 2023.

**Notes.** I also created the empty features folder, as the brief asked. During my one mesh-area run (about 1 s, under 100 MB), free memory read 1.79 GB, below the 3 GB wait threshold. I did not touch skin_build.py or skin.npz. Scratch work is in %TEMP%\p2prep_hair.
key_values: blender=5.2.1; representation=hair curves (no particles), guides + GN Interpolate Curves children, tactile = explicit curves; mystacial=12/side 4 rows x 3 arcs, lengths 30-66 mm (photo longest >=61 mm projected), base D=0.0023L+0.056 mm (rat Belli 2017, low conf) 125-212 um, taper ratio 7-13 (W&K 2010), Cesaro curvature flat base (Luo&Hartmann 2023), follicle depth 3 mm est; supraorbital 2-6/side 18-35 mm; genal 1-3/side 20-40 mm; chin 2-5 8-18 mm; carpal 4-6 20-30 mm (IMAIOS); ear furnishing 11 mm (7-16) 5-50/mm2; ear tip wisp 5-8 hairs 2-4 mm protrusion (no lynx tuft); inner pinna sparse 0.5-5/mm2 1-3 mm; ear canal 0; body density back 93/mm2, belly 186/mm2 ([C] + growth-mass bracket 47-95/mm2); type split guard 0.05 awn 0.11 down 0.84; group 19 hairs, spacing 0.45 mm; total ~23 M hairs on ~2150-2350 cm2 skin (Tripo envelope 2527 cm2); face photo scale 0.35-0.38 mm/px (coat.json 0.27 disagrees); legs/paws WHITE in photo
open: No measured cat vibrissa base diameter found (rat relation used, low confidence); Dougill et al. 2023 J Morphol and Noel & Hu 2018 SI Table S4 were 403-blocked - worth a manual fetch by the person
Cat hair density per area still rests on a [C] popular source plus an estimated growth-mass bracket
Photo scale disagreement: 0.35-0.38 mm/px at the face (eye spacing / frozen camera) vs coat.json 0.27 mm/px - orchestrator to reconcile
Photo shows legs/paws white (lynx point with white), contradicting the brief's point list
Interpolate Curves node availability on Blender 5.2 not yet verified (read-only node listing before build)
Mystacial per-row split and row length factors, supraorbital/genal/chin counts, follicle depth, down/awn diameters, colour band positions are estimates
Ear backs unseen in the photo (colour by colourpoint rule); caudal-thigh lilac patch may be tail-colour spill
Full real density (~23 M strands, ~4 GB curve data) does not fit the 16 GB box at once - T2 render uses a measured f_down for the undercoat, the one stated exception
Free memory was 1.79 GB (<3 GB) at the one 1-second area computation (<100 MB); skin agent's run is memory-heavy
